 New federal student loan requirements could impact certain UA programs
 Olivia Eastridge , Chief Copy Editor 
 October 21, 2026 
 CW / Hannah Grace Mayfield A sign for the Student Financial Aid and Scholarships office, photographed on Oct. 15, 2026, in the Student Services Center. 
 The University of Alabama was named Alabama’s #1 Best Value University for in-state students for 2027. With in-state tuition, housing and food totaling nearly $30,000 , however, this value comes at a significant cost. Around 33% of University students take out federal student loans each year to pay for these school-related expenses. 
 The William D. Ford Direct Loan program allows students at participating universities, including the University, to borrow money directly from the U.S. Department of Education through its federal student loan program. Under the department, the Office of Federal Student Aid funds nearly $121 billion in student loans, grants and work-study programs each year, according to its website . 
 “Our family has gone to college since my great-grandfather, but all of that is only possible because of student loans,” said Ava Gibbs, a senior majoring in history and art history. 
 Gibbs said she and many of her friends rely on student loans, whether private or federal, to pay for their tuition at the University. She said federal loans specifically are “especially helpful for when you come from an underprivileged family” because of their low interest rates. 
 For some students, however, federal funding may soon be withheld after the Department of Education announced its new “ Student Tuition and Transparency System ,” or STATS, in June of last year. This July, the new ruling introduced an accountability framework for participating universities, requiring undergraduate programs to prove their graduates earn more than a typical high school graduate in order to receive funding. 
 MaLea Cook, a junior majoring in graphic design, said federal student loans played a crucial role in paying for her freshman year. Since then, she has been awarded several scholarships to offset the cost of tuition. If the government cuts down on federal student loans, Cook said that she believes scholarships should be more accessible. 
 “I don’t think that students should have to prove they’re earning enough money to get money from the government because the government should give money anyway,” Cook said. “It’s what the government is for — to support the citizens.” 
 Similarly, Gibbs said that the government has a duty “to ensure that its population has access to education and access to relatively affordable education.” 
 While the new framework doesn’t directly include specific programs to be impacted, concerns have been raised about how humanities and fine arts degrees might be targeted. The five lowest median-earning degree programs at the University four years after graduation include human development and family studies at $45,751, English at $44,278, studio art at $41,100, anthropology at $35,701 and music at $31,666. 
 Gibbs said even for students who may not be majoring in the arts, humanities or social sciences, receiving a well-rounded, holistic education is important, and cutting student loans could lead to cutting funding for entire programs in the future. 
 “It is harmful because when you cut [funding for] these programs, you cut them not just for the students who are majoring in them, but you cut them for all,” she said. “Once you lose professors, you lose assistant professors. After that, all you have left are instructors, and those general education requirements are going to go.” 
 If a university program fails to prove graduates have earned a financial return on investment for two out of three consecutive years, it may lose eligibility to participate in the federal Direct Loan program. 
 “The University continues to evaluate the new federal rule and available federal earnings data to best meet the new demonstration requirements,” said a spokesman for the University, Alex House, in a statement regarding STATS’s impact. “A degree from The University of Alabama is a sound investment for students that provides financial and career advantages that extend across UA’s academic portfolio.” 
 Among the University’s top-earning bachelor’s degrees four years after graduation include computer science at $115,980, management information systems at $105,393 and chemical engineering at $100,857. 
 “Along with career advancement and financial security, the value of a UA education includes the intellectual capacity, creativity, and professional expertise that sustain Alabama’s economy, communities, and civic life,” House said. 
 Gibbs said the value of education, especially at The University of Alabama, cannot always be determined by statistics. 
 “[The government is] looking at it from such a numbers standpoint,” Gibbs said. “We shouldn’t just be measuring things by how productive they can be because productiveness for society does not always come from money.”
